29 A parallel beam of light of wavelength 600 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating.
The distance between adjacent slits in the grating is 2.0  10–6
m. A screen is placed parallel to
the grating, at a distance of 1.50 m from the grating. Third-order diffraction maxima are observed
at the two ends of the screen, as shown.

hints: Notice the given numbers for third order: $n = 3$, $\lambda = 600\text{ nm}$, slit spacing $d = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$, and grating to screen distance $1.50\text{ m}$.
Use the grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ for $n = 3$ to find $\sin\theta$, which is $0.9$ here and so $\theta$ is large and the small-angle approximation cannot be used.
Find the distance $y$ from the centre of the screen to one end with $\tan\theta = y / 1.50\text{ m}$, then double $y$ because the screen spans the upper and lower third-order maxima.
walkthrough: Write the diffraction grating condition for normal incidence: $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $\theta$ is the angle of the $n$th order from the central maximum.
Use the right-angled triangle to the screen: $\tan\theta = y / 1.50\text{ m}$, where $y$ is centre to one third-order spot. So $y = 1.50 \times 2.06 \approx 3.1\text{ m}$.
The two ends are symmetric above and below the centre, so total separation $= 2y \approx 6.2\text{ m}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too small. It is much less than twice the centre to third-order distance for $\sin\theta = 0.9$ with a $1.50\text{ m}$ grating to screen distance.

B.explanation: Too small. It is close to only one side distance from the central maximum to one third-order maximum, not the full end-to-end distance.

C.explanation: This is the distance from the central maximum to one third-order maximum, about $3.1\text{ m}$, not the distance between the two opposite third-order maxima.

D.explanation: Correct. With $\sin\theta = 0.9$, each third-order spot is about $3.1\text{ m}$ from the centre, so the separation is about $6.2\text{ m}$.
